question: Thierry Mariani is subject to Ukrainian sanctions under Decree No 726/20221, which are in force until 19 October 2027 and include a ban on entering Ukrainian territory. Ukraine is, however, an EU candidate country since 28 February 2022, and an EU-Ukraine far-reaching and comprehensive free trade agreement was concluded on 29 October 2025. Mr Mariani is therefore unable to carry out monitoring, control and dialogue missions, which form part of his parliamentary duties as a MEP. 1.

Does the Commission consider the fact that an EU candidate country is preventing a MEP from stepping foot on its territory to carry out his mandate to be compatible with the Statute for Members of the European Parliament?

Does it intend to raise this matter with the Ukrainian authorities to ensure that MEPs, including Mr Mariani, are not hindered from carrying out their missions related to the accession process and the free trade agreement?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (18.2.2026) Decisions concerning the adoption and implementation of restrictive measures by Ukraine are taken under its national legal framework and generally fall within its sovereign prerogatives.

It should also be noted that the statute of Member of the European Parliament does not grant the right to enter a third country, as access remains subject to that country’s applicable laws and decisions of its authorities. Concerns against such Ukrainian measures should, in the first place, be brought before the competent Ukrainian public authorities.
